correctness.rationale: Checked the frozen universal statement for fixed oriented simply-connected N with boundary S3, nonzero x of divisibility d and both knots in H1(Sigma_d)=0. Pencovitch Theorem 1.1 supplies the iff positive-genus threshold. Conway–Orson–Pencovitch Theorem 1.1 independently confirms the exact genus-zero criterion: M<=b2 and, only for characteristic x, Arf(K)+ks(N)+(sigma(N)-x.x)/8=0 mod2; minus/plus of that last integer are equivalent mod2. The homology condition excludes Alexander roots at nontrivial d-th roots, so the source signature and Powell's averaged signature agree there; at 1 both knot signatures are zero. Powell Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.4 give |sigma(K#-J)|<=2h in the locally flat topological category, with knot nullity beta=0. Thus each affine-signature coordinate and hence M changes by at most 2h. For integer h, the ceiling-half map changes by at most h and max with 1 preserves this for positive genera. If one genus is zero and h>=1, M(other)<=b2+2h gives G(other)<=max(1,h)=h. If h=0, signatures and Arf are concordance-invariant, so the zero branch agrees. This also handles d=1. A crossing change supplies a genus-one cobordism. The finite checker is unnecessary to the universal proof and was not executed.
